data.one_liner: A Flutter implementation of React hooks for managing widget life-cycle and code reuse.
data.what_it_does: It introduces a new kind of object (hooks) that manage the life-cycle of a widget, allowing you to extract and share stateful logic like AnimationControllers across widgets without using complex mixins.
use_when: You want to share stateful logic across multiple widgets without boilerplate.
You prefer a hooks-based architecture similar to React inside Flutter's build methods.
avoid_when: You rely heavily on standard StatefulWidget structures and do not want to adopt a hooks paradigm.
You are working with complex conditional hook calls (hooks must be called unconditionally).
strengths: Increases code-sharing between widgets by removing duplicate lifecycle boilerplate.
Extracted logic can be easily packaged and published independently.
weaknesses: Requires strict adherence to rules (calling hooks unconditionally and prefixing with 'use').
Hot-reload behavior can cause hard-resets of hooks if hooks are removed or reordered incorrectly.
